Strategy buys 811 BTC for $65.5M, holds 849,327 BTC total According to an SEC Form 8-K filed on November 2, Strategy purchased 811 BTC for approximately $65.5 million between October 26 and November 1, at an average price of $80,846 per BTC. As of November 1, the company held 849,327 BTC, acquired for a total of approximately $64.08 billion at an average cost of $75,451 per BTC. During the same period, Strategy sold approximately 1.18 million shares of MSTR common stock, generating $164 million in net proceeds, of which $65.5 million was used to purchase Bitcoin and $98.5 million was allocated to USD Cash. The company also repurchased approximately 2.09 million shares of its STRC preferred stock for $208.2 million. — link

BitMine adds 8,573 ETH, holdings reach 6.06M ETH BitMine said it acquired 8,573 ETH over the past week, bringing total holdings to 6,060,506 ETH, or about 4.9% of Ethereum’s supply. The company has 5,227,037 ETH staked, while total crypto, cash, marketable securities and other investments stand at about $14.5 billion, including $498 million in cash and marketable securities. — link

Mercado Bitcoin confirms cyberattack, Hypernative estimates over $40M suspected losses Mercado Bitcoin, Brazil's largest cryptocurrency exchange, confirmed on November 2 that one of its systems had suffered a cyberattack. The exchange said the incident was quickly contained, customers would not incur losses, and no customer data had been leaked. Deposits and withdrawals have been temporarily suspended as a precaution. Tether said it has frozen more than 4.5M USDT related to this security incident. According to preliminary analysis by blockchain security firm Hypernative, more than $40 million in suspicious transfers were identified across at least 10 blockchains, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, and Tron. The estimated losses have not been confirmed by the exchange, and the attack method remains unknown. Brazilian crypto exchange Mercado Bitcoin said approximately $38 million in assets were involved in the security incident. Working with Tether, Circle, Paxos, BRL1, and Chainalysis, the exchange has blocked approximately $11 million and identified additional assets that may be eligible for blocking. Containment efforts remain ongoing. Mercado Bitcoin reiterated that customers will not suffer asset losses and said services will resume once security conditions are fully met, with no timeline announced. — link

CryptoCom to Discontinue Consumer App in Hong Kong on February 1, 2027 According to Bloomberg, CryptoCom will discontinue its consumer app in Hong Kong effective February 1, 2027, citing efforts to optimize global operations and resource allocation. The company said affected users have been notified and will receive instructions on account closures and fund withdrawals. Meanwhile, CryptoCom continues to pursue a virtual asset trading platform license from Hong Kong's Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) through Foris DAX HK Limited for its institutional-grade CryptoCom Exchange platform. — link
